sentences.text:
This is an appeal filed by the Insurance Company u/S 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 being aggrieved the award dated 22.07.2017 passed by IVth Member Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
(Link Court) Badanwar, District Dhar, [in short "Claims Tribunal"] in claim Case No. 289/2015 seeking exoneration from its liability to pay compensation to claimants on the ground of false implication of offending vehicle in the alleged accident.
2. Brief facts of the case are that on 23.09.2010, Kanhaiyalal @ Kaniram (since deceased) was going on his motorcycle bearing Registration No.MP 09 MM 4514 along with his brother Babulal.

sentences.text: On the way, driver of another motorcycle bearing Registration No. MP 11 MG 6020 driving in rash and negligent manner, dashed the motorcycle of deceased, as a result of which, he sustained grievous injuries on his body.
He was taken for NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:35301 2 MA-2867-2017 treatment to hospital where during treatment he died on 30.09.2010.
On the same day, District Hospital sent information to police station concerned.

The claimants/respondent Nos.
1 to 4 filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the appellant/Insurance Company and rest of the respondents before the Claims Tribunal seeking compensation regarding death of the deceased in the alleged accident to the tune of Rs.40 lacs.

sentences.text: 3. The Insurance Company as well as driver and owner of the offending vehicle filed reply and denied claim averments.
4. The learned Claims Tribunal framed issues.

After hearing the pleadings of both parties and material/documents available on record, allowed the claim petition of claimants and awarded Rs.7,22,694/- in their favour, which shall be paid by the Insurance Company and respondent Nos. 5 & 6 (driver and owner of the offending vehicle), jointly and severally.
5.
Being aggrieved by impugned award, the Insurance Company filed this miscellaneous appeal on the ground that FIR was lodged after 51 days of the incident.
The delay was not properly explained by the claimants.
The incident took place on 23.09.2010 whereas, FIR was lodged on 14.11.2010 to secure compensation from the Insurance Company by claimants.
The claimants, in collusion with owner as well as driver of offending vehicle have falsely implicated.

It is further submitted that in the MLC (Ex.P-5), it was written by Dr. Chobe that deceased sustained injuries due to fall off from his own vehicle and the same fact has already been mentioned in medical document (Ex.P-105).
The Claimants Tribunal has ignored this NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:35301 3 MA-2867-2017 aspect while passing the impugned award.
The record shows that the cause of death of the deceased was not due to offending vehicle, but the deceased had sustained injuries himself due to fall off from his own motorcycle.
Hence, the Insurance Company is not liable to pay any compensation amount to the claimants and the Insurance Company deserves to be exonerated from its liability.
6. On the other hand, learned counsel for the claimants contended that the Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation and argued in support of the findings recorded by the Tribunal.

7. Heard the arguments advanced by the counsel for the parties and perused the record of the Tribunal.
8.
On perusal of the record of Claims Tribunal, it is found that the incident took place on 23.09.2010 in between 8:30 - 9:00 AM.

The deceased was admitted in the hospital on the same day and he was died during treatment on 30.09.2010 by which, an information was sent by the District Hospital to police station concerned on 30.09.2010.
On the basis of such merg intimation, FIR at Crime No.378/2010 was registered by the concerned police station.
On completion of investigation and other formalities, the charge-sheet was filed against the driver of the offending vehicle.
9. The contention of the appellant/Insurance Company that FIR was lodged with the police station concerned with delay of 51 days and the delay has not been properly explained.

On perusal of medical documents Ex.P-5, it is found proved that the accident occurred on 23.09.2010 and merg intimation was recorded on 30.09.2010, whereas the MLC was done on the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:35301 4 MA-2867-2017 same date of accident.
FIR was lodged on the basis of merg intimation on 14.11.2010 by the concerned police station.

10. In other words, although, lodging of FIR is vital in deciding motor accident claim cases, delay in lodging the same should not be treated as fatal for such proceedings, if claimant has been able to National Insurance Company Ltd. vs Smt. Chandabai on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65053947/
2 demonstrate satisfactory and cogent reasons for it.

sentences.text:
Apex Court in case of Ravi Vs. Badrinarayan and Others AIR 2011 SC 1226 in para 20, 21 has held as under:-
"20.

entities.text: Ravi Vs. Badrinarayan and Others AIR 2011 SC 1226
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is well-settled that delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt the claimant's case.
Knowing the Indian conditions as they are, we cannot expect a common man to first rush to the Police Station immediately after an accident.
Human nature and family responsibilities occupy the mind of kith and kin to such an extent that they give more importance to get the victim treated rather than to rush to the Police Station.
Under such circumstances, they are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging the FIR with the Police.
Delay in lodging the FIR thus, cannot be the ground to deny justice to the victim.

In cases of delay, the courts are required to examine the evidence with a closer scrutiny and in doing so;
the contents of the FIR should also be scrutinized more carefully.

If court finds that there is no indication of fabrication or it has not been concocted or engineered to implicate innocent persons then, even if there is a delay in lodging the FIR, the claim case cannot be dismissed merely on that ground.
21. The purpose of lodging the FIR in such type of cases is primarily to intimate the police to initiate investigation of criminal offences.
Lodging of FIR certainly proves factum of accident so that the victim is able to lodge a case for compensation but delay in doing so cannot be the main ground for rejecting the claim petition.

In other words, although lodging of FIR is vital in deciding motor accident claim cases, delay in lodging the same should not be treated as fatal for such proceedings, if claimant has been able to demonstrate satisfactory and cogent reasons for it.
There could be variety of reasons in genuine cases for delayed lodgment of FIR.
Unless kith and kin of the victim are able to regain a certain level of tranquility of mind and are composed to lodge it, even if, there is delay, the same deserves to be condoned.
In such circumstances, the authenticity of the FIR assumes much more significance than delay in lodging thereof supported by cogent reasons."
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:35301 5 MA-2867-2017 11.

In the motor accident case of any, member of a family of the claimants has died, it cannot be expected that first, they should rush to the police station and lodge the report immediately after the accident, human nature and family responsibilities occupied in mind give more importance to the victim's treatment, rather than to rush to the police.
So, it reveals that as per record, date of accident was 23.09.2010 and information sent to the police by hospital on the same day and deceased was died during treatment on 30.09.2010.
So, there is no delay in lodging the FIR, it is found that explanation of delay in the FIR is sufficient, therefore, on the basis of delay in the FIR, claim case cannot be discarded.

12. The next contention of the counsel for appellant/Insurance Company that in MLC (Ex.P-5), it was mentioned by doctor that accident occurred due to fall off from his own motorcycle and in document (Ex.P- National Insurance Company Ltd. vs Smt. Chandabai on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65053947/
3 105), it was also mentioned that deceased was riding the motorcycle and fell on the road due to slip of his own motorcycle.

13. On perusal of medical documents, it appears that the alleged accident took place due to road traffic and it was obligatory on the part of the Insurance Company to put question in regard to his defence before Doctor - Sachin Adhikari (AW-2) before the Claims Tribunal, who exhibited the Ex.
(P-105).
But, appellant had no dare to put these questions before (AW-2) Dr. Sachin.
So, his defence was not proved.

14. Considering the findings of the Claims Tribunal, it was found that Claims Tribunal has elaborately discussed this point and found that accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:35301 6 MA-2867-2017 15.
In view of aforesaid discussion, it is found that Insurance Company has utterly failed to prove that the alleged accident occurred due to fall off from his own motorcycle by deceased.
It cannot be said that the offending vehicle has been falsely implicated in the alleged accident.
The Insurance Company cannot be exonerated from its liability to pay compensation as awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal in favour of the claimants.
16. Accordingly, this appeal being devoid of substance, is hereby dismissed.
as per rules.
